name: Ride a bike with no hands
blurb: A small, satisfying party trick that teaches you how bicycles actually balance — through steering geometry and hips rather than arms.
gear: A wide, empty, smooth space with no traffic
steps: Get comfortable riding one-handed first, both sides, including looking over your shoulder.
Sit upright and shift your weight back slightly so the front wheel is lightly loaded.
Ride at a decent speed — slow is much harder — and hover your hands just above the bars before letting go.
Steer with your hips and by leaning, and keep pedalling smoothly. Coasting makes it harder.
Build from a second to ten seconds, then add gentle turns.
Learn to get your hands back on the bars smoothly rather than grabbing.
tips: Do it away from traffic, kerbs and pedestrians until it is reliable.
A bike with a loose headset or twitchy steering makes this far harder than it should be.
proof: Fifty metres hands-free, including a gentle turn in each direction.
